summary: The right valuation tool (mid-cycle) and a good quarter support it, and the order is already the smallest. But the stock has doubled off its low on war-elevated oil, and oil is falling fast on peace talks.

thesis.text: APA is valued on a mid-cycle cash-flow model, so the value does not rely on today's oil price. Expected value is about 36% above the price, and the bear case is still slightly above it.
Q3 beat on production: US oil output was 128k bbl/d, 4k above guidance. The quarter produced $699m of free cash flow, $537m was returned to shareholders, and debt is down $2.8bn since end-2024.
The stock trades at about 3x EV/EBITDA, and consensus also sees upside. Energy ranks 3rd of 11 sectors.
The proposed order is the smallest of the four, at about 5.3%.

red_team.text: Brent was about $89.6 on 10 November, down nearly 24% since the start of the month on US-Iran diplomacy hopes. APA's Q3 cash flow was earned at much higher prices.
The stock is about 100% above its 52-week low, so much of the war premium may already be in the price that a deal would remove.
Its 45% standalone volatility is the highest of the four orders. Even at 5% weight it takes about 20% of portfolio risk.
The OPEC+ ministerial on 29 November could schedule the unwinding of about 2m bbl/d of cuts, a supply risk for 2027 prices.
Valuation confidence is the lowest of the four orders, and about 70% of the value is terminal.

what_would_change.text: A signed US-Iran deal with Brent heading toward the $70s, as the EIA projects a year out, would move this to CHALLENGE unless the mid-cycle value is re-checked.
Waiting until after the 29 November OPEC+ meeting is a reasonable alternative to approving now.
